  4. Repeat, then tallyStop at absorption or either slab boundary.

Behind the Computation Live execution, without the black box

The actual algorithm

for each independent history ID:
  RNG ← hash(seed, history ID)
  x ← 0; direction ← (1, 0, 0)
  u ← uniform in (0, 1)
  flight ← −ln(u) / Σt
  if boundary comes first: escape
  else draw v:
    v < p_absorb → deposit E; stop
    otherwise → isotropic direction
  repeat; tally final outcome

10,000 collisions is a safety cap. Capped histories retain residual energy and are reported separately.

UNDERSTAND THE EXPERIMENT

One history is simple. A billion is a workload.

Each particle takes a different random walk. More histories reduce statistical noise, approximately as 1/√N. Independent histories can be distributed across CPU threads and cluster processes.

What is physically coherent?

This is a homogeneous, infinite lateral slab with vacuum boundaries at x = 0 and x = thickness. Flight distances follow an exponential distribution. At a collision the particle is absorbed, or scatters elastically and isotropically in 3D. Energy remains constant until absorption. Escaped, deposited and capped residual energy sum to the incident energy.

What is simplified?

Material presets are illustrative coefficients, not cross-section libraries. The photon option is an elastic surrogate, not Compton or photoelectric transport. No secondary particles, energy-dependent data, charged-particle stopping, dose conversion or medical interpretation. Use a validated transport package for scientific predictions.

What do the colors mean?

Green: forward escape. Pink: absorption. Violet: backward escape. Amber dots: scattering. Final outcomes are mutually exclusive. A transmitted particle can have scattered many times. Tracks are projected in 3D and visually offset along the source to separate them. Transverse extents are clipped for display; the model slab is laterally infinite.

Reproducibility

The seed and global history ID initialize a 32-bit random stream. Worker counts do not change that stream. Browser checkpoints keep completed chunk IDs; interrupted chunks are recalculated on resume. Native and JavaScript implement the same model and RNG, but floating-point math across platforms can differ near decisions. This educational RNG has not been certified for production radiation analysis.

How to tell an honest scaling story

Use identical physical parameters, seed and history count for strong scaling. Repeat measurements, report medians and the range, and keep compilation and runtime labels. A larger worker count may be slower because startup, scheduling, contention and reductions cost time. A browser cannot measure whole-system CPU load; its occupancy value measures worker activity only.
